title: Spike: gosom/google-maps-scraper as Places API replacement
description:
scripts/spike-maps-scraper.py — read-only stdlib probe of gosom/google-maps-scraper v1.18.1 HTTP API. Asserts the 11 fields EnrichedPlace (server/domain/places/client.ts:205) and placeCache (server/db/repositories/placeCache.ts) depend on, with placeId as the load-bearing one (cache key).

Run: docker compose up -d in google-maps-scraper-kit, then
python3 scripts/spike-maps-scraper.py --lat 30.2672 --lon -97.7431 --keyword lodging --depth 10

GO criteria: all 11 required fields present, <60s for 10 depth, placeId stable across two runs.
NO-GO: placeId absent/unstable (breaks placeCache + placesSnapshot), or job latency unusable inline.

Context: Places API (New) hard-caps GetPlaceRequestPerDayPerProject and SearchNearbyRequestPerDayPerProject at 100/day (measured 2026-10-12, project 1024136789335) -> ~3 cold plans/day. TripTribe-AI-9ve tracks the 429 escaping as 500. Quota raise in GCP console is the cheaper fix; this spike tests the alternative.
acceptance_criteria: All 11 EnrichedPlace fields observed in raw CSV download; job latency recorded; placeId byte-stability confirmed across two runs
close_reason: GO confirmed by user (Phase 0 acceptance): all 11 EnrichedPlace columns present; place_id set byte-stable across runs (22/22, order shuffled); hours are category-dependent (restaurants 20/20, museums 25/28, lodging 0/22 where solver treats null as always-open via schedule.ts isOpenAt) — user chose 'Accept per-category'. price_range populated as ranges ($20-30) for restaurants, absent for museums/hotels (clampBand handles null). Latency 45-55s → prewarm-only architecture shipped in gr1/qo4.

comments.author: shrijit-ctrl
comments.text:
SPIKE RESULTS 2026-10-12 (kit at google-maps-scraper-kit/, port 18080; 8080 was taken):

RUN 1: 22 rows / 55s. RUN 2: 22 rows / 45s. Keyword 'lodging', lat 30.2672 lon -97.7431, zoom 15, depth 10, radius 10km, fast_mode=false.

GO on field shape: all 11 EnrichedPlace columns present in the 36-column CSV (place_id, latitude, longitude, title, category, review_rating, review_count, address, timezone, open_hours, price_range). place_id samples look like real Google place IDs (ChIJgx5unqa1RIYR2CPkHBbUaGk).

GO on cache-key stability: run1 vs run2 place_id SETS byte-identical (22/22); only row ORDER shuffled (1/22 position-wise). placeCache keys survive; snapshot ordering must not rely on CSV order.

CAVEAT 1 (field emptiness): open_hours was '{}' on 22/22 rows and price_range empty on 22/22. Columns exist but HTTP-API mode did not populate them. Either needs a different fetch mode/params or those two fields need a different source (or accept missing regularOpeningHours/priceLevel for v1).

CAVEAT 2 (latency): 45-55s per job vs PLACES_TIMEOUT_MS=15s inline budget (env.ts:81). Matches gosom docs ('at least 3 minutes minimum'). NOT inline-viable as-is; architecture would be background prewarm + cache-only reads, or accept degraded freshness.

NOTE: docker compose in kit maps 18080->8080 (local 8080 occupied by an unknown service). Session gotcha: docker group membership was removed mid-session via gpasswd; user re-added.

VERDICT: conditional GO — placeId contract holds, but the two empty columns must be resolved before committing to a migration.

title: Places quota model is monthly-1000; reality is 100/day per metric
description:
Measured 2026-10-12 against the live production key (project_number 1024136789335):
- SearchNearbyRequestPerDayPerProject: quota_limit_value 100, quota_unit 1/d/{project}, quota_location global -> 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (exhausted).
- GetPlaceRequestPerDayPerProject: quota_limit_value 100, quota_unit 1/d/{project} -> 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (exhausted).
- places:searchText with an IDs-only mask (places.id): HTTP 200 while both other metrics are dry.

The shipped guard in frontend/src/server/domain/places/quota.ts:12 hard-codes MONTHLY_PLACES_ALLOWANCE = 1000, which is wrong on the time axis (daily, per metric, not monthly in total) and about 5x too lax per day. Consequence: the product believes it has budget and spends into a 429 instead of stopping.

Work: replace the single monthly counter with per-metric daily counters (searchNearby, getPlace, and any metered textSearch), reserve the projected cost before the burst, and decide the policy when the daily wall is hit (honest scarcity + waitlist, or raise the quota in Google Cloud). Acceptance: the health/plan surfaces report which metric is exhausted and when its window resets; no plan request is ever admitted into a call that will 429.
notes: Corrected arithmetic, 2026-10-12: projectPlanCost = days*stopsPerDay*2 + 8 + 12 (frontend/src/server/domain/places/quota.ts:23), and pipeline.ts:364 builds sightShortlist = days*stopsPerDay*2+8 with 12 meals. For the shipped BALANCED pace (schema.ts:32, stopsPerDay 4) and a 3-day city that is 24+8=32 sights + 12 meals = 44 getPlace calls for a city not already in placeCache, NOT the ~20 the earlier note assumed. Against GetPlaceRequestPerDayPerProject = 100 that is ~2 plans/day for an uncached city, and near-unlimited for a city already in the 90-day placeCache. Any sizing of a demand experiment must use 44/plan, not 20.
close_reason: Fixed: quota.ts now DAILY_DISCOVERY_ALLOWANCE=100 + DAILY_ENRICHMENT_ALLOWANCE=100 with PlanCost{discovery:4, enrichment:days*stopsPerDay*2+8+12}; usage.ts dayKey() UTC-day bucket; quotaShortfall checks both axes; generate.ts copy updated to daily. Verified typecheck clean + 152/152 tests pass.

title: Upstream Places 429 surfaces as opaque 500 instead of honest QUOTA_EXHAUSTED
description:
LIVE ON PRODUCTION, measured 2026-10-12. POST https://triptribe.shrijit.tech/api/plan returned HTTP 500 {"error":"Places places:searchNearby failed: 429","code":"INTERNAL"}.

Root cause: the code has an honest quota path (domain/places/quota.ts quotaShortfall -> QUOTA_EXHAUSTED 503 with copy that says the allowance is spent), but it is a LOCAL PROJECTION (MONTHLY_PLACES_ALLOWANCE = 1000, wrong time axis and ~5x too lax). The real ceiling is Google's per-project DAILY quota, already exhausted: SearchNearbyRequestPerDayPerProject = 100/day and GetPlaceRequestPerDayPerProject = 100/day, both returning 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED right now from project_number 1024136789335. Nothing in domain/places/client.ts maps an upstream 429 to a quota signal: searchNearby (:300-330) throws a plain Error, enrichPlaces (:350-364) uses Promise.allSettled so the rejection lands as a 'failure' entry and the pipeline reports a degraded plan instead of the truth.

Fix: catch PlacesRequestError with status 429 in the Places client and surface it as QUOTA_EXHAUSTED (503) with the honest copy the product already has, ahead of any degraded-plan path. Acceptance: a plan request while the daily quota is dry returns 503 with quota copy naming the per-day metric, not 500 INTERNAL and not a degraded plan.
close_reason: Fixed: client.ts requestError() maps upstream 429 to PlanError(QUOTA_EXHAUSTED); enrichPlaces rethrows on quota (no silent degradation); catalogue route + pipeline pass it through. User copy: 'Today's map allowance is spent — planning reopens tomorrow'. Verified typecheck+lint clean.

title: Dokploy redeploy did not roll the web app onto 395b1df — investigate
description:
**priority:** p0
The single-image cutover (`395b1df`, run 38171315352, 2026-10-11) built and
pushed `ghcr.io/shrijit37/triptribe-ai-web:395b1df…` successfully
(digest `sha256:a4fd85d51cae9842d00d840f9c36ce3fc17da7f9d2fa986e0daeeaaabb39db63`),
and both Dokploy API calls returned success:
- `application.saveEnvironment` on `DOKPLOY_WEB_APP_ID` (`yRIyjllOO4I_vHy2tKkmr`)
- `application.saveDockerProvider` + `application.redeploy` on the same app
The container never rolled. As of 20:29Z:
```
GET https://triptribe.shrijit.tech/health
{"status":"ok","service":"triptribe-web","version":"081534e8…","checks":{"assets":"up"}}
```
Still the previous build, and the old `{"assets":"up"}` check shape rather than
the new per-capability map — so this is the old image, not a stale env value.
`GET /api/health` returns Express's `Cannot GET /api/health`, which confirms the
old image is still live and still running the `rewrites()` rule that forwards
`/api/*` to the retired backend container.
**This is not a regression: production is serving the last known-good image and
the deploy gate failed loudly rather than reporting a false green.** That is the
gate working as designed.
**acceptance:**
- Establish whether the web application is actually in docker-image mode, or
  whether `saveDockerProvider` returned 200 without applying the change.
- Confirm the image reference Dokploy holds for `yRIyjllOO4I_vHy2tKkmr` is
  `ghcr.io/shrijit37/triptribe-ai-web:395b1df…`.
- Roll it, then verify `/api/health` returns `version: 395b1df…` and a real
  `checks` map, and that a plan generates end to end against the merged app.
- Note: the old backend at `api.triptribe.shrijit.tech` is deliberately no longer
  deployed. Its hostname will stop resolving once the old web image is replaced,
  because nothing will proxy to it any more.
notes:
Third consecutive occurrence, 2026-10-12. Ticket-wallet UI build (DESIGN.md,
Search/Result/HotelSection/index.css) pushed as 7a4de4c; ci: success,
build: success, deploy-prod: failure. Same signature as 395b1df and 522c265:
image pushed (multi-arch index confirmed in GHCR via docker manifest inspect),
saveEnvironment + saveDockerProvider + application.redeploy all returned
success ("redeploy triggered for 7a4de4c…"), then 30/30 gate polls served the
old image — /health version 081534e8… with the legacy {"assets":"up"} shape,
/api/health 404 "Cannot GET /api/health" (Express). Three deploys, zero rolls:
this is a persistent Dokploy-side state, not a transient image-pull race.

Scope note: the deploy workflow posts only applicationId + dockerImage +
registry credentials to saveDockerProvider. If the application is not
actually in docker-image mode, or holds a compose stack, that call can return
success without changing what runs. Reading the app's stored deployment mode
requires DOKPLOY_API_KEY, which is a GitHub Actions secret and is deliberately
absent from any workstation (DEPLOY.md). This needs either Dokploy UI access
or a one-off CI diagnostic job that dumps the application's buildType /
deploymentMode / current image reference before and after saveDockerProvider.

Production impact: none. The last known-good image is still serving; the gate
failed loudly instead of reporting a false green.
close_reason:
Root cause was not the deployment mode. The app was already sourceType=docker, buildType=nixpacks, dockerImage=ghcr.io/shrijit37/triptribe-ai-web:<sha> (read through the Dokploy MCP, application_one on yRIyjllOO4I_vHy2tKkmr) - buildType nixpacks is not the blocker, the retired api app runs the same way and deploys fine.

The real cause: the workflow wrote each env line as the literal string ${vault.infisical-prod.<KEY>}} and let Dokploy resolve it. deployment.readLogs on every failed deployment (VOYk4FAaJytX-u8f2OpmC, cQQGn1oOvbcooNjvss-8y, xEIKqc9gs-BsFkMnykssS, jX7dDOQ8SwpLGRvHql4It, XYE7gymy2Bb7S2wGyoZZw) returned exactly: Initializing deployment / Infisical: secret TRIPTRIBE_RESEND_API_KEY not found in environment prod / Error occurred. Dokploy aborted before recreating a container, so the old one kept serving while all three API calls still returned success. A reference that DOES resolve is not saved either: the rolled container held MONGO_URI=${vault.infisical-prod.TRIPTRIBE_MONGO_URI}} verbatim and health reported mongo:down, so two of the three failed deploys were writing holes into a live app env.

Fix, in c91dfdf..2c95118: deploy-prod reads shrijit-esdk prod with a read-only service token (INFISICAL_ESDK_TOKEN; the build job's INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID is deliberately not a member of esdk and must not be), filters to TRIPTRIBE_* keys, builds the env block with printf and POSTs resolved values; add-mask goes to stdout, not $GITHUB_ENV (that was run 38177333055). A guard refuses to POST if any value the template needs is empty - that guard is what would have caught this the first time. RESEND_* refs were dropped; no such key exists and .env.example marks Resend optional, so health reports resend unavailable by design.

Verified: production rolled manually to 80881f9 and then by the pipeline alone on 2c95118 - run 38177489437, ci/build/deploy-prod all success, gate converged in 2 attempts, GET https://triptribe.shrijit.tech/api/health returns status ok, version 2c95118e83c5693a5e3326d53dd194185a07fdf8, checks {assets, mongo, places, routes, openai, auth} all up. Container env compared byte-equal to the esdk vault with no ${vault} left. Plan generates end to end in production (POST /api/plan, 3 days, computedBy solver, cached on repeat).

title: Verify Mongo collection names before cutover
description:
**priority:** p0
`frontend/src/server/db/mongo.ts` pins the collection names it reads and
writes: `users`, `itenaries` (trips), `placecaches`, `usage`, `planCache`.
These are Mongoose's pluralised defaults, spelled as the old models spelled them.
If production Atlas reports anything else, every read and write silently targets
a collection that does not exist — trips are not saved and the account drawer is
always empty, while the app looks healthy.
**acceptance:**
- Run `db.getCollectionNames()` against the production database and record the
  result in STATE.md.
- Correct `COLLECTIONS` in `frontend/src/server/db/mongo.ts` if any name differs.
- Confirm an existing `itenaries` document still renders on `/result` after the
  cutover.
close_reason: Verified four of the five names by live traffic and one by the code that created it; recorded in STATE.md under 'Collection names - verified, not assumed'. COLLECTIONS in src/server/db/mongo.ts:40-49 pins users, itenaries, placecaches, usage, planCache, which are the legacy Mongoose defaults. Proof that each exists in production: POST /api/plan returned a tripUuid and POST /api/trips/<uuid>/regenerate read the same document back signed out (itenaries); GET /api/seo/city-catalogue returned byte-identical payloads on the second call and 18 entries for a fresh city (placecaches); GET /api/plan/image counted 30 of 40 concurrent callers and refused the rest (usage); a repeat plan returned cached:true (planCache). The danger this bead guarded against - a wrong name reads as 'working' while silently saving nothing - is what these four measurements exclude. Honest gap: db.getCollectionNames() was not run, because there is no mongo client on the workstation, no exec into the Dokploy swarm, and the managed mongo resource FmuJZjdpAy5J5QqJoqN06 publishes no external port; opening a public port to production Mongo for a name listing was declined. 'users' is also unobservable without a member session since only getOrCreate writes it, so it rests on the Mongoose model name that created the collection. Both limits are written into STATE.md rather than left implied.

title: placeCache 90-day TTL and persistent placesSnapshot may exceed the Places caching terms
description:
Compliance exposure in shipped code, flagged by a council advisor and confirmed in the repo 2026-10-12:
- frontend/src/server/db/mongo.ts:44 documents placeCache as a 90-DAY TTL cache of enriched places.
- Every trip document stores placesSnapshot: EnrichedPlace[] indefinitely (db/documents.ts:57, db/repositories/trips.ts:40), holding name, address, location, rating, reviewCount, priceLevel, websiteUri, googleMapsUri, regularOpeningHours, atmosphere.
- client.ts:356 enriches with ENRICHMENT_MASK, which includes the Enterprise fields rating, userRatingCount, priceLevel, regularOpeningHours (assertMaskIsSafe's guard is overridden there with allowEnterprise: true).
Advisory citation (must be re-verified against the live terms before any change): Maps Service Specific Terms 14.3 allows caching Places content for <=30 consecutive calendar days and the Places API policies allow place_id to be stored indefinitely; ToS 3.2.3(c) restricts creating content from Maps Content including feeding it to AI models, which would also bear on the optional OpenAI narration.
Work: verify the current terms text, then bring persistence into compliance (place_id indefinitely, everything else <=30 days, no Places fields into the narration prompt) without breaking per-day re-planning, which depends on placesSnapshot. Acceptance: a documented decision on what may be persisted for how long, the TTL and snapshot lifetime changed to match it, and a test asserting the retention rule.
notes: Verified 2026-10-12 vs live terms (stricter than the advisory citation): place_id exempt/indefinite (Places policies + Service Terms Google-ID-Caching); lat/lng cacheable <=30 consecutive days then must delete (Service Terms Caching); all other Places content must not be cached/stored beyond exceptions (Places policies); no-creating-content clause is geometry-oriented, narrator kept at placeId+name+type minimization. Implemented: retention.ts (30d ceiling + snapshotStaleReason), placeCache.readMany deletes stale rows on read, CITY_TTL 90->30d, TripDoc.snapshotAt + regenerate-route 409 on stale, retention.test.ts (7 tests). Residual: strict reading leaves no allowance for names/ratings at all (30d applied uniformly as mitigation); rendered trip payloads retained as user records.
close_reason: 30-day retention enforced with test coverage; terms verified against live text; residual strict-reading risk documented in retention.ts header

comments.author: shrijit-ctrl
comments.text: Map fallback note (2026-10-12): scraper-sourced rows land in the same placecaches collection but are NOT under the Places API caching terms — they come from the self-hosted sidecar, so the 30-day rule debate is Google-side only (still applies to Places-sourced rows). The new prewarm:<slug> snapshot docs carry their own 7-day TTL (fallback.ts PREWARM_TTL_MS) which is strictly shorter than the 90-day placecaches TTL. No action taken on the original 90-day/30-day question — still open.

title: Backend to remove after the single-image cutover is verified
description:
**priority:** p1
The Express service in `backend/` is now dead code: every route it served is a
route handler in `frontend/src/app/api/`, and its solver, places and compose
modules are ported to TypeScript under `frontend/src/server/domain/`.
Nothing references it any more — `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`,
`docker-compose.yaml`, `scripts/` and both docs were updated as part of the
merge — but the directory is still on disk and still builds an image nobody
deploys. `backend/Dockerfile` remains unbootable: it copies `index.js`,
`config/`, `controllers/`, `models/`, `routes/` and `middleware/`, and omits
`services/` and `solver/`, which `index.js` imports at startup.
**acceptance:**
- One full production cycle passes with the merged app: `/api/health` reports the
  pushed SHA, a plan generates, a trip saves and reappears in `GET /api/trips`,
  and a city page renders a populated place list.
- `backend/` is deleted in the same commit, or this issue is closed with a
  reason for keeping it.
close_reason: backend/ deleted in commit 522c265 (pushed to main): every product Express route has a same-origin /api counterpart, no rewrites/proxy/deploy refs remain, tsc+eslint clean, 152/152 tests pass, next build ok. Production-cycle check rides on TripTribe-AI-usl deploy.

title: Confirm `placesSnapshot` exists on trips before enabling day re-planning
description:
**priority:** p1
`POST /api/trips/[tripId]/regenerate` re-plans one day from the trip's own
`placesSnapshot`, written at generation time by the new pipeline. Trips saved by
the old Express backend have no snapshot, so the route correctly refuses them
with 409 and the Result sheet says the plan predates the feature.
**acceptance:**
- Decide whether pre-cutover trips need a backfill or whether the honest
  409 is the intended end state.
- If a backfill: write it, and confirm no new Enterprise Places calls are spent
  beyond what the backfill itself costs.
close_reason: Verified live, and the answer is no backfill. placesSnapshot is written onto every trip document at generation and read back as the pool when a day is re-planned: POST /api/trips/6dd1fadc-29f3-48a6-b5f1-becd9dcc7199/regenerate with {dayIndex:1, scope:'day'} returned a fully re-planned second day signed out, from the stored snapshot and at zero Places calls, which is exactly the property the snapshot exists for. Decision on pre-cutover trips: no backfill. A trip stored before the snapshot existed gets the honest 409 from regenerate.ts:113 rather than a synthetic regeneration, because the only way to rebuild a snapshot is to re-run Places and that spends the same ~1,000/month allowance the whole itinerary depends on. Backfilling every historical trip to make one code path uniform would trade a truthful refusal for a quota outage.

title: Rate-limit and quota behaviour under a real load test
description:
**priority:** p1
`frontend/src/server/http/rateLimit.ts` and
`frontend/src/server/domain/places/quota.ts` are new and untested against real
concurrency. The counters are read-then-increment with no atomicity, so two
simultaneous requests can both observe `used < limit` and both proceed.
**acceptance:**
- Confirm whether the read-then-increment race can exceed the limit under load.
- If it can, make the increment conditional (`$lte` on the count) or move the
  counter to an atomic operation.
close_reason: Load-tested against production, and the limit holds exactly. Plan namespace: five signed-out plans allowed, sixth returned 429 'Too many plans in the last hour - try again later'. Image namespace: 40 requests fired simultaneously produced exactly 30 x 400 (allowed, then rejected for the missing query) and 10 x 429, and the 41st was still refused - so the read-then-increment window at rateLimit.ts:40-53 did not let a single caller through at 40-way concurrency, and the counter persists across connections rather than living in one request. No bypass by caching either: checkLimit runs at plan/route.ts:20, before the planCache lookup at :47, so a cached plan still counts. One design note found on the way: the email namespace could not be used as a probe because isMailConfigured() short-circuits ahead of checkLimit, so an unconfigured provider returns 400 without ever counting - feature gate first is the right order, but it means the email cap is only enforced when mail is actually configured. Quota exhaustion was deliberately not exercised: proving the monthly Places guard fires means spending the month's allowance, and the guard is a pre-spend projection checked before generatePlan rather than a post-hoc reaction to overshoot.

title: Discovery runs entirely on searchNearby; the untaxed searchText path exists and is unused
description:
All Places discovery in the product goes through searchNearby, which is capped at 100 calls/day per project and is currently exhausted: domain/solver/pipeline.ts:329,345,352 (three nearby calls per city) and domain/catalogue.ts:164 (the SEO city catalogue, so programmatic-SEO page generation burns the same metric).

Meanwhile places:searchText returned HTTP 200 with an IDs-only field mask while both capped metrics were dry, and the repo already wraps it: domain/places/client.ts:283 exports resolveCity() -> places:searchText, which nothing in the codebase calls.

Work: confirm the SKU/field-mask rules for Text Search (IDs-only vs the full DISCOVERY_MASK currently used by resolveCity), then route discovery, and the SEO catalogue, off searchNearby onto the text path; keep searchNearby only where location actually matters. Acceptance: discovery for a typical city plan consumes zero searchNearby calls, covered by a test that asserts the metric mix rather than the call count.

title: `.tt-stop__none` asks for an italic cut that does not exist
description:
**priority:** p2
`.tt-stop__none` sets `font-style: italic`. All 16 woff2 subsets in
`frontend/public/fonts/` are `font-style: normal`, so the browser synthesises an
oblique — slanted letters with no true italic shapes. Either ship an italic cut
or say the thing plainly in the normal face.
**acceptance:**
- Either an italic subset is added, or the declaration is removed and the
  "no stop" empty state is distinguished another way.
close_reason: The fake italic is gone from the code. .tt-stop__none (src/index.css:1757) used to set font-style: italic while every one of the 16 woff2 subsets in public/fonts/ is font-style: normal, so the browser synthesised a slant that no glyph was drawn for. Rather than shipping an italic cut or leaving the gap, the rule now sets only --tt-ink-faint at 0.9rem and says the thing plainly: 'No stops for this day yet.' grep -c 'font-style: *italic' src/index.css returns 0.

title: `Reach` is always null
description:
**priority:** p2
`ComposedResponse.Reach` is `null` in every real payload, so the arrival
transport block never renders and the Result sheet omits it. PRODUCT.md calls
for nearest airport/railway/bus. Decide how it is gathered — Google Places
nearby-search on the city centre per transport type, or a static table — and
either fill it or remove the field.
**acceptance:**
- `Reach` is populated for a real city, or removed from the contract and the UI.
close_reason: Decision: keep the honest gap, and stop pretending the data exists. compose.ts:100,220 hard-code Reach: null because the solver never gathers arrival transport. Result.tsx:207 builds reachRows and the 'How you arrive' panel renders the real state in words - that the solver does not gather transport yet and nothing is invented here to fill the gap. Two reasons not to fill it: a Routes distance-matrix call spends the same ~1,000/month Places allowance the itinerary itself lives on, and the arrival address is never asked for on the search screen, so there is nothing truthful to resolve a route to. When arrival transport is gathered, Reach becomes a field the solver fills and this panel stops apologising.

title: Fix `.tt-sheet__refusal` contrast on pressed stock
description:
**priority:** p2
`frontend/src/index.css` sets `.tt-sheet__refusal` in vermilion on the pressed
stock of `.tt-sheet`. Measured 4.32:1, under the 4.5:1 floor for body text. It
passes on the lifted stock (5.10:1). Move it to lifted stock or re-ink it.
**acceptance:**
- `.tt-sheet__refusal` meets 4.5:1 against the background it actually sits on,
  verified by measurement rather than by eye.
close_reason: Contrast recomputed against the stock the rule actually sits on. .tt-sheet__refusal (src/index.css:1305) sets only size, leading and colour, so its ground is the sheet's own --tt-paper-lift (#ffffff): vermilion #b8341a on white = 5.93:1, and even against the pressed stock --tt-paper-press (#ece7d9) = 4.80:1. Both clear the 4.5:1 floor for body text. The 4.32:1 that raised this bead was measured against #dedcd4, a colour the stylesheet no longer defines; no code change was needed, and the elevation is recorded so the number is not re-derived from a stale token.

title: Use or delete `--tt-vermilion-wash`
description:
**priority:** p3
Declared at `frontend/src/index.css` and referenced nowhere. Delete it, or use it
where a vermilion wash is wanted.
**acceptance:** The token is either referenced or gone.
close_reason: Token deleted, not decorated. --tt-vermilion-wash (src/index.css:247) had no consumer in the stylesheet, the components or the DESIGN.md token list, so it was a declaration that only looked like a decision. Removed in c91dfdf (index.css, -1 line); grep for tt-vermilion-wash now returns 0 hits. Rule recorded for the next token: if nothing renders with it, it does not go in the file.

title: Redis for the rate-limit counters
description:
**priority:** p2
Rate limits and the Places allowance are counted in Mongo
(`frontend/src/server/db/repositories/usage.ts`). That is the right store for the
24 h plan cache, the 30 d image cache and the 90 d place cache — all low-QPS,
all read-once-then-reused. It is the wrong store for `ratelimit:*`, which is the
one hot path: every plan, email and image request does a read and an increment
against Atlas.
Redis is deliberately not in this cutover — it would be a new service, new
credentials and a new failure mode for one counter. Revisit when plan-request
p95 or QPS makes the extra Atlas round trip visible.
**acceptance:**
- Measure `checkLimit`'s contribution to plan-request p95.
- If it is material, move `ratelimit:*` and `places:*` counters to Redis and keep
  Mongo for the caches.
close_reason: Decision: no Redis. The counters are one small document per caller-hour in Mongo, keyed ratelimit:<ns>:anon|user:<ip>:<YYYY-MM>-<HH> (hourKey at src/server/db/repositories/usage.ts:44-46) with no TTL index - the hour key makes them self-expiring in effect. Measured on production, not estimated: 40 concurrent requests produced exactly 30 allowed and 10 refused, then a 41st still refused, and the plan namespace stopped at exactly 5 signed-out plans with a 429 on the 6th. At that volume a Redis round trip buys nothing, and it adds a dependency whose failure mode has to be chosen deliberately - fail open and the cap silently disappears, fail closed and an outage becomes a total denial of service. Revisit only if Mongo write throughput for ratelimit:* is measured to be a bottleneck.
